Priya Gupta: hey all :wave: I'm Priya, started today on infra. Trying to bootstrap inside the company devcontainer (Ubuntu 22.04). Running into an issue installing python via asdf: `openssl` error during build. Steps I did: installed asdf, added python plugin, `asdf install python 3.11.6` — it fails with OpenSSL 1.1 vs 3.0 errors. Also my dotfiles symlink script errors with `cp: cannot create symbolic link ...` when run inside the container. Any pointers?

Jules Tran: welcome! :tada: For python/asdf in a container you usually need the build deps. Try:
```
apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \n  build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libbz2-dev libreadline-dev libsqlite3-dev libncurses5-dev libgdbm-dev liblzma-dev
```
That fixed it for me on similar images.

Sam Lee: if you're hitting OpenSSL API removal (OpenSSL 3) you can either install libssl1.1 compatibility or point Python to the right OpenSSL during configure. Example envs:
```
export LDFLAGS='-L/usr/lib/$(uname -m)-linux-gnu'
export CPPFLAGS='-I/usr/include'
PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS='--with-openssl=/usr' asdf install python 3.11.6
```
Works in a pinch.

Priya Gupta: tried the apt packages, still seeing build fail with 'undefined symbol: EVP_MD_CTX_reset' at the end. Last lines:
```
_build/temp.linux-x86_64-3.11/_ssl.c:...: undefined symbol: EVP_MD_CTX_reset
error: command 'gcc' failed with exit code 1
```

Jules Tran: that's the OpenSSL 3 API change. Options: install libssl1.1 compatibility package, downgrade to a python version with prebuilt binaries, or use the distro python. For devcontainers we usually pick a distro-backed Python (apt) or use a prebuilt pyenv/ASDF binary. Also for symlinks use `ln -sfn` instead of `cp` when provisioning dotfiles as non-root user.

onboarding-bot: onboarding docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/onboarding/dev-setup — contains recommended devcontainer image and steps for asdf/python/dotfiles.

Sam Lee: for your dotfiles script, ensure $HOME is correct and the entrypoint doesn't run as root unless you mean it to. `ln -sfn` is idempotent; if `cp` is failing because target exists as a dir, `ln -sfn` will replace. Also consider running `chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) $HOME` in the container step if files are owned by root.

Priya Gupta: switched to distro python for now and updated dotfiles to `ln -sfn` — container boots fine. One quick question: who do I request 1Password access to infra vaults from?

Jules Tran: ping #help or mention @oncall-ops in the ticket; include your manager and the repo/team name.

Priya Gupta: awesome, thanks everyone! I'll file a short note in the onboarding doc about the OpenSSL gotcha so new hires don't stumble on this. :thumbsup:
